name: Israeli occupation zone in southern Syria
summary: Since Assad's fall Israel has occupied the UN buffer zone on the Golan, the Syrian side of Mount Hermon and positions deeper in Quneitra and Daraa, raiding villages and striking Syrian forces. It also acts as protector of Sweida's Druze, flying equipment into the province.

sides.name: Israel
sides.strength: Positions in the former UN buffer zone, Mount Hermon, and inside Quneitra and Daraa provinces; no unit numbers retrieved.

sides.name: Syrian state and local residents
members: Syrian Interior Ministry forces (lightly armed in the south under Israeli demilitarisation demands)
sides.strength: Israel demands the south be demilitarised, limiting Syria to lightly armed Interior Ministry forces (Jerusalem Post, 26 Oct 2026).

background: On 8 December 2024 Israel declared the 1974 disengagement agreement void and moved troops into the demilitarised buffer zone and onto Mount Hermon. Over the following year the UN logged about 900 Israeli ground incursions in Quneitra and Enab Baladi counted about 830 air raids across Syria. Israel says it is preventing hostile forces and weapons from reaching its border; Damascus calls it an occupation. US-mediated security talks in 2025 did not produce an agreement.
year: On 28 November 2025 an Israeli arrest raid in Beit Jinn on the slopes of Mount Hermon turned into a firefight that killed 13 Syrians and wounded Israeli soldiers. Netanyahu visited Israeli-held Syrian territory on 19 November 2025 and pledged to protect the Druze. On 20 March 2026 Israeli jets struck government positions at Izraa in Daraa during fighting in Sweida. Incursions and detentions continued (e.g. two people detained in Quneitra on 20 May 2026), and in October 2026 Israel was reported to be building up in Sweida province and airlifting hardware to hills held by the Druze National Guard, while a Syrian was killed in a raid in mid-October, sparking protests.
situation: Israel holds a strip of southwestern Syria along the Golan, including the Hermon summit, and patrols and raids villages beyond it. It demands a demilitarised south and is extending a military presence toward Sweida. There is no Israel-Syria security agreement.
technical: About 900 Israeli ground incursions in Quneitra from Dec 2024 to end-2025 (UN HRC via EUAA).
About 830 Israeli air raids and 15 artillery bombardments in the year after Assad's fall (Enab Baladi via EUAA).
Israeli-held areas in the south remained outside Syrian government control as of Feb 2026 (UN HRC via EUAA).
Israel built positions inside Quneitra and Daraa as a precursor to a military line parallel to the Golan (The National, 22 Oct 2026).
Helicopter resupply of Sweida over the Yarmouk River basin; surveillance and radar equipment dropped on hills (The National).
Beit Jinn raid 28 Nov 2025: 13 killed (BBC via EUAA).
casualties: No cumulative figure retrieved; incidents include 13 killed at Beit Jinn (28 Nov 2025) and one Syrian killed in mid-Oct 2026 (EUAA; Jerusalem Post). Estimated well under 100 deaths in the 12-month window.

timeline.event: Netanyahu visits Israeli-held Syrian territory and pledges to protect the Druze.
Beit Jinn raid and firefight kill 13 Syrians.
Israeli strikes on Syrian army positions at Izraa, Daraa.
Israel reported airlifting equipment into Sweida province.

outlook: Watch for a formal Israel-Syria security arrangement (blocked partly by Sweida), any Israeli base inside Sweida province, and clashes if Syrian troops move against the Druze National Guard.

battles.name: Israeli strikes on Syrian army positions at Izraa
battles.outcome: Israel hit government positions including 40th Battalion facilities after government-Druze fighting in Sweida on 19 Mar.
battles.significance: Confirms Israel's standing policy of striking Syrian forces that press the Druze, which caps Damascus's options in Sweida.

battles.name: Israeli raid and firefight at Beit Jinn
battles.outcome: Israeli arrest raid met armed resistance; Israeli strikes followed.
battles.forces: IDF ground raid force with air support.
battles.significance: Deadliest single incident of Israel's occupation of southern Syria in the window and a sign of growing local armed resistance near Mount Hermon.
